To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fluctuations of particle multiplicities in Au+Au collisions at FAIR energy are expected to be sensitive to the phase transition and critical point in the QCD phase diagram.

the fluctuations of the ratios of the particle multiplicities, and the total positive to negative charges, in central Au+Au collisions at FAIR energies, exhibit a non-monotonic behavior as a function of time.

(i) Fluctuations of particle multiplicity, their ratios and the ratio of total charge at the ﬁnal state of the collision are sensitive to the initial conditions of the collision and to the time evolution of the system; (ii) The time evolution of these ﬂuctuations are diﬀering from each other and also from the time evolution of ﬂuctuation measures like the skewness and kurtosis of the particle multiplicity and their ratios.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of ﬂuctuation observables at FAIR energies.
the investigation of the propagation of ﬁuctuations of particlemultiplicities, their ratios and the ratio of total charges in AuAu collision at E = 2.4 GeV usingthe UrQMD hybrid model.

the investigation of the propagation of the event-by-event ﬂuctuationsof particle multiplicities, and their ratios and the ratio of total charge of positive and negative particles inAuAu collisions at the beam energies available at FAIR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study shows that the ﬂuctuations in the particle multiplicities and the ratio of positive and negative charges are sensitive probes to the exotic phenomena like phase transition and/or critical point.
the propagation of the fluctuations in Au + Au collisions at FAIR energy is not very much dependent on the initial time of the fluctuations.

the present work has been able to show that the propagation of the event-by-event ﬂuctuation of particle multiplicitiesand their ratios is a sensitive probe to the exotic phenomena like phase transition or the occurence ofcritical point at the early stages of the collision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ﬂuctuations at freezeout are not thesame as those at initial stage.
the ﬂuctuations are found to show a non-monotonicbehaviour with time in the early stage of the collisions, however, this behaviour disappears in the laterstage of the collisions.
the ﬂuctuations at freezeout is a function ofﬂuctuations at the time of the occurence of the phase transition or critical point.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the propagation of ﬁnite size ﬂuctuations from early times to the freeze-out time is very important in order to extract the physics at the early times from ﬂuctuationmeasurements at freeze-out.
the ﬂuctuations are not only sensitive to the freezeoutconditions but also to the time evolution of the system.
the ﬂuctuations are not only a measure of the initial conditions but also of the dynamical processes which occur in the system during its evolution.
